solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Irish writer trapping silly Charlie in futile enterprise

indicators.note: trapping means the writer's name closes round the other pieces

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Dublin-born playwright
a goose is a silly person, so silly gives goose
Chas is the short form of Charles, Charlie's full name

explanation.surface: An Irish author holds some foolish chap captive during a pointless project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like the NATO-alphabet C, but here it is CHAS, the old written short form of Charles; 'silly' is a noun-like GOOSE, a foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a hopeless pursuit of something unattainable, hence any pointless undertaking.

clue.text: Candle nearly out, in part of Ireland

parts.note: the wick is the burning part of a candle, standing in for the whole
a flame burning low is nearly out

explanation.surface: A guttering candle somewhere in rural Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a picture of a candle burning down: WICK and LOW together describe it exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: County Wicklow lies south of Dublin on Ireland's east coast.

clue.text: Party hard, using lots of staff

parts.note: the Labour Party, one of Britain's main political parties
intensive work is hard, concentrated work

explanation.surface: A political party working hard and deploying a big workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party hard' suggests a night out; LABOUR is Britain's main left-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: A process described this way needs a large workforce relative to its capital or machinery.

clue.text: Resounding blow gets a medal

definitions.meaning: a struck disc that rings out loudly, as in a dinner bell signal
British slang for a decoration or award

explanation.surface: A ringing punch earns someone a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The struck metal disc gives the first sense; British slang uses the same word for a military or civil decoration.

clue.text: Group of people exhausted by sudden attack

parts.note: exhausted means used up, finished, so out
a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing

explanation.surface: A team worn out after a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a team, firm or band of people working together is called this.

clue.text: Fire up underground worker who asks tough questions?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to fire someone is to axe them
a miner works below ground

explanation.surface: A mine worker set to grill people with hard questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire up' looks like a phrasal verb meaning excite; split it, AXE for fire, turned by 'up' in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone setting a test poses difficult questions to candidates; the question mark marks the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Hurried to introduce key point, tough and realistic

indicators.note: to introduce means the hurrying word takes the others into its middle

parts.note: hared means ran fast, hurried
D is a musical key
a head is a point of land, a headland

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to make a crucial point, being shrewd and pragmatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key point' reads as one phrase meaning the crux, but it splits in two; 'to introduce' means the hurrying word takes both inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical, unsentimental person is described this way; it is a direct synonym for shrewd realism.

clue.text: Kind of guarantee covering all cases that's comforting

definitions.text: Kind of guarantee covering all cases
definitions.meaning: read literally, a security that is blanket, applying to every situation
a cherished object, like a child's blanket, that soothes anxiety

explanation.surface: An all-inclusive guarantee sounds reassuring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like an insurance policy; the literal sense is an all-embracing security, the idiomatic one a child's comfort object.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's familiar blanket, or anything that reassures someone anxious, is an object that soothes.

clue.text: Like a granny, perhaps, difficult to deal with

definitions.meaning: a granny is a kind of tied loop, which sailors consider poorly made
a problem described this way is tricky and complicated

explanation.surface: A grandmother who is awkward to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny is a type of tied loop in rope, and a tangled, intricate problem is described with the same adjective.

clue.text: It can be unorthodox for assembled ministers

indicators.note: unorthodox means not in the usual order, so the letters of the three opening words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cabinet minister remarking that the government can be unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior ministers of a government meeting together form this body.

clue.text: Day in a US prison for person from continent

indicators.note: in means the day is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: can is American slang for jail
Fri is short for Friday

explanation.surface: Someone from abroad spends a day locked up in an American jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the day between the article and the jail; the jail word is American slang, not British.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Africa, the continent, is a native of that landmass.

clue.text: Yob left before getting dismissed

indicators.note: before means the left letter comes ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A thug left before being thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A yob is a British word for a rough, uncouth young man; both are synonyms for a hooligan.

clue.text: Cut off, some island is in her itinerary

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller's planned route includes an isolated island, cut off from the mainland.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone off, in the will sense, is to deprive an heir of an inheritance.

clue.text: Not easily disturbed, so unaffected by live wire

definitions.meaning: describing a calm person, or a device resistant to jolts
safe from electric jolts when touching a current-carrying cable

explanation.definitionFit: The word means resistant to jolts or impact, and read literally it means immune to electric jolts from a live cable.

clue.text: Importance of women's crew

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on a clothing label
a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: How much a women's rowing crew counts for.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that carry importance carry this; influence and significance are synonyms.

clue.text: They should pay landlord any rent, as arranged, on time

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Tenants ought to pay their landlord whatever rent was agreed, promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as arranged' looks like 'as agreed' about the rent, but it shuffles ANY RENT, then T for time follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective body of renters on an estate owes rent to the owner of the land.

clue.text: Still wild, and in one piece

definitions.meaning: a horse not yet tamed or trained to the saddle

explanation.surface: Something remains untamed, and also intact.
explanation.definitionFit: An untamed horse has never been trained by a rider; an intact object has never been smashed.

clue.text: Secretive, taking it back in late

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the other piece

parts.note: recent and late both mean of a short time ago

indicators.note: taking, paired with back, signals that the little word is retracted, read in reverse
back says the short word is written from right to left

explanation.surface: A secretive person recalling something lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'back' together turn the little word round, and 'in' places the result inside the word for late.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reserved and unwilling to reveal much is keeping things to themselves, close to secretive.

clue.text: Run old companies in old-fashioned style

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
Co is short for company, so two companies give it twice

explanation.surface: Managing aged firms in a dated manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornate eighteenth-century decorative style, now also used loosely of anything fussy and dated.

clue.text: Boys like Basil, for instance?

parts.note: Herb is a boy's name, short for Herbert
Al is a boy's name, short for Albert or Alan

explanation.surface: Lads who resemble someone named Basil.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil looks like another boy's name alongside the boys, but it is the plant, an example of a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a culinary plant, so it is of the kind used for seasoning or remedies.

clue.text: Wise King Edward

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic monarch
Ned is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: A sagacious monarch named Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly, knowledgeable person is erudite, close in sense to wise.

clue.text: Do some damage in Chartres cathedral

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of letters of the place name and building

explanation.surface: Vandals harm the great French Gothic church at Chartres.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to harm or injure, surviving in unscathed.

clue.text: Plot, with prisoners, a crime

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
piracy is a crime at sea or of copyright

explanation.surface: Inmates scheming over an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret plan by several people to do wrong is a plot or scheme.

clue.text: A delay held back a sporting event

indicators.note: held back means the pieces are written in reverse

parts.note: a lag is a delay or time lapse

explanation.surface: A sports fixture was postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' looks like 'postponed', but it turns A LAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: A British swimming gala is a competitive meeting of races, a sports occasion.

clue.text: OK one form of punishment

definitions.meaning: a monetary penalty for an offence

explanation.surface: Approval of one kind of penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a word for satisfactory and a sum paid as a penalty share the same spelling.

clue.text: Fabric acceptable for American Indian

parts.note: chino is a cotton twill fabric used for trousers
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: Cloth deemed suitable for a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinook are a Native American people of the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Reduce, as cook, disorder in kitchen

indicators.note: disorder means the letters of the following word are thrown into a jumble

explanation.surface: A cook boils a sauce down amid chaos in the galley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduce' as a cook means boiling a liquid down to concentrate it, which makes it denser.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook reduces a sauce to make it denser; the culinary sense of reduce is to boil until it gets more viscous.

clue.text: Nobody else could be so concerned about personal gains

definitions.text: Nobody else could be so concerned about personal gains

parts.words: Nobody else could be so concerned about personal gains
parts.note: someone focused only on their own advantage cares about it more than anyone else could

explanation.surface: Only one person could care this much about their own advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A person driven by personal advantage is selfish and motivated by private gain.
